title: Design and validate assessment, test, and audit strategies
question: Which assurance activity, scope, criteria, and independence are credible for this claim?
scenario: Leadership asks whether privileged cloud access is safe.
focalRelation: leadership claim --defines--> criteria and scope criteria/scope --select--> assessment, executed test, or audit test result --supports observed behavior only--> evidence set audit --uses defined criteria and sufficient independent evidence--> bounded conclusion

nodes.label: Privileged cloud population
nodes.detail: Named accounts, roles, regions, paths, and time period to which the safety claim applies.

nodes.label: Control claim
nodes.detail: The question “Is privileged cloud access safe?” decomposed into lifecycle, authentication, authorization, monitoring, and review criteria.

nodes.label: Assessment criteria
nodes.detail: Explicit required behavior and failure conditions against which evidence is evaluated.

nodes.label: Independent assessor
nodes.detail: Reviewer with enough objectivity and authority to challenge owners and report limitations.

nodes.label: Evidence set
nodes.detail: Configuration, account population, exceptions, observed access paths, logs, and representative samples.

nodes.label: Bounded conclusion
nodes.detail: Finding that names supported controls, exceptions, excluded paths, sampling limits, and the decision it informs.

edges.label: defines population from which evidence is selected
supports conclusion only for stated scope and limits

states.title: Case facts fixed
states.caption: Leadership asks whether privileged cloud access is safe.

states.title: Controlling condition identified
states.caption: Assessment is the broad decision activity; testing is a method; audit emphasizes independence and criteria.

states.title: Tempting shortcut rejected
states.caption: A penetration test is the same as an audit. A penetration test explores technical exploitability; an audit evaluates evidence against defined criteria and independence requirements.

statuses.n1: password scan covers only one path

states.title: Bounded action applied
states.caption: Define accounts, roles, regions, time window, control criteria, evidence sources, sampling, assessor independence, and report decision. A password scan alone cannot answer the governance and lifecycle question.

statuses.n5: configuration, sample, exceptions, and logs tested

states.title: Outcome accepted with limits
states.caption: Choose an assessment strategy for a stated control question and explain its scope, criteria, evidence, independence, and limitations. The case record retains the scope, owner, exceptions, and evidence used for this conclusion.

statuses.n6: conclusion bounded to named population and period

variants.label: Changed case
variants.changedFact: A manager requests a full-security conclusion from a one-day vulnerability scan.

states.title: Changed case fact isolated
states.caption: A manager requests a full-security conclusion from a one-day vulnerability scan.

states.title: Decision recomputed
states.caption: Narrow the conclusion to the scanned scope and method, or design a broader program. Evidence cannot support claims beyond population, time, and method.

statuses.n3: scan criterion covers technical exposure only

states.title: Changed outcome verified
states.caption: The decision remains provisional until the changed dependency, enforcement result, and accountable evidence are verified.

nodes.label: One-day scan scope
nodes.detail: The observed population and time window cover only systems reached by the scan.

nodes.label: Full-security claim
nodes.detail: Management asks for a conclusion broader than the method can support.

nodes.label: Scan criteria
nodes.detail: The method checks selected technical exposures, not every control or operating period.

nodes.label: Assurance owner
nodes.detail: The assessor must preserve independence and state scope and limitations.

nodes.label: Vulnerability scan evidence
nodes.detail: The evidence shows findings and nonfindings only within the scanned scope.

nodes.label: Bounded scan conclusion
nodes.detail: The report limits the conclusion or requires a broader assurance program.

edges.label: bounds what scan evidence can show

prediction.prompt: Which assurance activity, scope, criteria, and independence are credible for this claim?

options.label: Limit the conclusion to the named accounts, regions, period, criteria, and tests
options.feedback: Correct for this scenario: this answer uses the displayed relation and preserves its scope. A penetration test explores technical exploitability; an audit evaluates evidence against defined criteria and independence requirements.

options.label: A penetration test is the same as an audit.
options.feedback: Incorrect: A penetration test explores technical exploitability; an audit evaluates evidence against defined criteria and independence requirements.

options.label: Treat the policy and leadership interview as proof that privileged cloud access is operating safely.
options.feedback: Incorrect: policy and testimony establish intent, not operating effectiveness. The conclusion needs scoped configuration, population, event, exception, and independent test evidence.

prediction.hint: Name the controlling relationship and the point where its result must be enforced; do not rely on a label or successful prior step.

transfer.prompt: A manager requests a full-security conclusion from a one-day vulnerability scan.

options.label: Reuse the original conclusion because the overall control family is unchanged
options.feedback: Changed fact: A manager requests a full-security conclusion from a one-day vulnerability scan. Why this answer fails: “Reuse the original conclusion because the overall control family is unchanged” does not account for that changed condition. Corrected consequence: Define accounts, roles, regions, time window, control criteria, evidence sources, sampling, assessor independence, and report decision. Repair target: Decision recomputed — Narrow the conclusion to the scanned scope and method, or design a broader program. Evidence cannot support claims beyond population, time, and method.

options.label: Narrow the conclusion to the scanned scope and method, or design a broader program
options.feedback: Correct. Narrow the conclusion to the scanned scope and method, or design a broader program. Evidence cannot support claims beyond population, time, and method.

options.label: Bypass the normal owner and apply a permanent broad restriction immediately
options.feedback: Changed fact: A manager requests a full-security conclusion from a one-day vulnerability scan. Why this answer fails: “Bypass the normal owner and apply a permanent broad restriction immediately” does not account for that changed condition. Corrected consequence: Define accounts, roles, regions, time window, control criteria, evidence sources, sampling, assessor independence, and report decision. Repair target: Changed outcome verified — The decision remains provisional until the changed dependency, enforcement result, and accountable evidence are verified.

transfer.hint: Trace the changed fact to the exact decision boundary, then identify the evidence needed before the outcome can be accepted.

retry.prompt: A penetration test excludes the payment processor API, yet the draft conclusion says the checkout service resists external attack. How should the conclusion change?

options.label: Infer the processor path is safe because the provider is certified and the tested application passed
options.feedback: A provider certificate and another path’s test do not establish this integration’s behavior.

options.label: Publish the broad conclusion and put the exclusion only in a technical appendix
options.feedback: A material scope limit must constrain the conclusion, not be hidden from decision makers.

options.label: Limit the claim to tested paths and state the excluded processor API, or add authorized coverage before broadening it
options.feedback: Correct. Assessment evidence supports only the defined scope and method.

retry.hint: The conclusion cannot be broader than the assets, paths, time, and methods actually examined.

takeaway: Define accounts, roles, regions, time window, control criteria, evidence sources, sampling, assessor independence, and report decision.
assumptions: The scenario is a bounded application of the canonical unit, not a universal threshold, legal conclusion, or vendor prescription.
Directed edges carry only their printed relation; proximity and shared color do not imply ownership, authorization, or chronology.
Acceptance applies only to the stated scope and retained evidence; unknown or excluded conditions remain explicit.

treatmentDispositions.rationale: Implemented in 5 stable decision states: Privileged cloud population defines population from which evidence is selected Evidence set; Control claim is translated into testable criteria Assessment criteria. The model keeps Privileged cloud population, Control claim, Assessment criteria, Independent assessor, Evidence set, Bounded conclusion distinct. Its changed case is “A manager requests a full-security conclusion from a one-day vulnerability scan.” and every option returns to a named repair state.

learningJob.plainExplanation: Assessment answers a bounded control question, testing supplies methods and evidence, and audit adds criteria and independence expectations. The conclusion must remain limited to the defined population, period, evidence, sampling, and assessor role.
learningJob.visualReasoningGain: A stronger comparison would align assessment, test, and audit against scope, evidence, criteria, and independence; the opening population/claim/criteria boxes do not enable that selection.
